Mahler coefficients on the two parity branches have unit/4-unit linear terms with nonlinear differences at least two or three valuation levels higher, yielding exact scaled isometries for every 2-adic input. The even-base remainder has exact valuation n-3 (odd n) and n-2 (even n), for all n>=7. An ultrametric minimum establishes all claimed nonresonant defects and strict resonance bounds; the threshold is sharp at N-1 and the odd branch forces the least period. A package-local Python checker passed 13,074 exact assertions through k=11, supplementary rather than proof.

originality.rationale: Kwong establishes the least eventual period, and Bennett–Mosteig explicitly establish stable parity-dependent valuation classes for the seventh Stirling column; both are credited rather than relabeled. Neither inspected work gives the exact transient defects at every n or the earliest periodic index for every binary depth. The 2014 published difference formula excludes columns 2^m-1 and hence k=7. published-finding corpus overlap comparisons were by object, shift parameters, quantifiers and mathematical implication, not merely title. value.rationale: The least period of a modular sequence does not identify its sharp first valid index. This theorem obtains exactly that natural cutoff for every binary depth in a historically exceptional Mersenne Stirling column, together with a two-scale exact transient defect law and the two precise cancellation-resonance boundaries. The result is a motivated structural refinement of established Stirling periodicity, not an arbitrary finite table or minor numerical improvement; unresolved resonance valuations are clearly bounded but not asserted as known.
